main_strengths: Strong school fidelity: every trajectory reasons via M2, MV=PY/velocity, long and variable lags, natural rate, rules vs discretion and credibility; no Keynesian multiplier or Austrian malinvestment drift
Consistent relative-price vs monetary-inflation distinction for supply shocks (oil, drought, freight, tariffs), a genuinely Monetarist move

Some event-specific gems: stablecoin as private near-money (syn-m0010), bank capital -> money multiplier (syn-m0006), freight shock with low M2 -> temporary (syn-m0014), mortgage relief financing channel (syn-m0017)
Most named analogs real and pre-2025 (1967 Suez, 1973/79/90 oil, Mexico 1994, Asia 1997, Argentina 2001, 2008 MMF run, 2022 stablecoin depeg, China RRR 2014-22)
Signals do vary with the snapshot's M2/inflation regime: bonds LONG in low-M2 disinflation cases, SHORT in high-M2 inflation cases
main_problems: Information leakage in ~17/20: the Think before get_macro_data already quotes snapshot values (M2, CPI, sometimes 2s10s/VIX), so the tool call is theatre; student will learn to hallucinate data before fetching

Gold LONG in 18/20, credit SHORT in 18/20 and equities SHORT in 17/20 (never LONG for any of the three), often regardless of base-case scenario: gold LONG under disinflation/benign bases (m0000, m0001, m0005, m0019) is a teacher default
Scenario probabilities weakly tied to signals: benign base cases (rule-anchored, temporary shock >=0.55) paired with conviction-4 risk-off signals (m0005, m0008, m0012, m0015)
US-style snapshot (core PCE, DXY, M2) silently applied to China/Japan/Asia/LatAm/EM events; region never questioned
Event-snapshot inconsistencies not flagged (m0002 '2.0pp above target' vs core PCE 6.2%; m0005 'inverted short-end' vs +216bp); event magnitudes (0.4pp RRR, 500bn, +0.3pp) rarely sized

Vague or fabricated analogs in a few items (m0015 unnamed shutdown episodes, m0017 'various episodes', m0019 1990s LatAm tariff escalation); analog descriptions often pre-written to confirm Monetarist priors

Template monotony: near-identical chains/analogs across geopolitical items (m0008/m0012/m0013); scenario labels recycle the same 4 archetypes (rule-anchored / accommodation / velocity collapse / credibility erosion)
Format drift: 3 scenarios in m0016, 'SHORT (3)' without 'conviction' in m0019, prompt leakage 'I must reason as a monetarist'
suggested_prompt_or_template_changes: Enforce tool-order integrity: forbid citing any snapshot number before the get_macro_data Observe (auto-reject via regex on numbers matching snapshot values before that step)

Require an explicit 'signal rationale' line per asset tied to a named scenario, and a check that the probability-weighted direction matches the signal; reject if base case is benign but >=3 risk-off conviction-4 signals

Remove default-asset bias: tell teacher gold/credit/equities have no default and require NEUTRAL when the chain gives no directional reason; monitor per-asset direction shares across the pilot and resample if >70% one way

Make the snapshot's economy explicit (add a 'region' field) or generate region-appropriate snapshots for China/Japan/EM/LatAm events; instruct the teacher to state how a foreign event transmits to the US snapshot (or vice versa)
Require the agent to size the event (bp, % of base money, pp) and to flag event-snapshot conflicts rather than ignore them

Require analogs to name country, institution and year; reject 'various episodes' or undated generic labels; keep the episode DB as a real tool with fixed returns so analogs are not teacher-confabulated
Positive-shock and benign templates (easing, RRR cut, mortgage relief) should be oversampled with snapshots where the Monetarist answer is risk-on, so the student sees LONG equities/credit cases
Fix output schema: exactly 4 scenarios summing to 1.0, 'DIRECTION (conviction N)' format, strip meta-phrases like 'I must reason as a monetarist'
Vary scenario taxonomy: ask for event-specific scenario names instead of the recycled rule/accommodation/velocity/credibility quartet
